newsitem.title: UK: Dollar and Eurobourses surge to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar and Eurobourses surge to new highs.

text.p: The dollar climbed to its highest levels against the mark and yen in years on Friday, helping to push German and French shares to record highs.
London shares also rose during the morning following Wall Street's recovery overnight, but like elsewhere, investors were wary ahead of crucial U.S. jobs data due later.

The dollar started on a strong footing in Europe on the expectation that the world's main industrialised nations would not try to shoot it down at this weekend's meeting in Berlin of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank governors.
The U.S. currency hit a high of 1.6645 marks during the morning, its highest level since June 1994. Against the yen, it hit a four-year peak of 124.40.
Traders and analysts said they did not expect either the employment data, due at 1330 GMT, or the G7 meeting to do much to sap the dollar's energy.

"People are thinking that if any statement does come out of the G7, it's more likely to suggest that the yen is too weak than to say anything about the dollar," said Pat Magill, head of corporate trading at Daiwa Europe.
U.S. non-farm payrolls, key data for indicating the strength of the U.S. economy, are forecast to have risen 237,000 in January after an increase of 262,000 in December.
Chase Securities said it expected the payrolls figure to be boosted by a smaller-than-normal decline in seasonal employment, helped by a mild winter.
German debt traded sideways during the morning, while British government bonds opened a little lower with traders waiting for the U.S. figures.
One broker said a payroll rise of less than 220,000 should allow bond markets to head higher.
Equity markets were all bolstered by Wall Street's renewed strength following Wednesday's 86-point slide, but investors looked unwilling to make any significant moves before the jobs data.
British shares pared some of their gains by midday following weaker futures, but bid talk continued to underpin sentiment, traders said.
The FTSE 100 index was up 15.5 points at 4,281.4 by 1230 GMT with gainers in a two-to-one majority.
"The cash market has been tracking the futures," said one trader. "But there's all sort of bid possibilities floating around that are helping the market."
Shares in investment bank Schroders and fund management group Mercury Asset Management were the latest stocks to benefit from bid speculation.
Traders cited talk of a bid from U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and Co Inc after this week's surprise merger between Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter Discover & Co.

The continuing strength of the pound provided some concern, however. On Thursday the Bank of England's trade-weighted index moved on Thursday to its highest level since the pound left Europe's exchange rate mechanism in 1992.
French stocks hit a fresh all time high of 2,577.13 points on the CAC-40 index before slipping slightly to 2,573 for a rise of 15 points by 1230 GMT.

Havas , suspended on Thursday, opened 1.71 percent ower at 441.30 francs and then lost another nine francs by midday. Generale des Eaux , also suspended on Thursday, opened up 2.18 percent at 750 and then surged to 772 francs for a rise of more than five percent.

The companies announced on Thursday that CGE would become the majority shareholder of Havas with 30 percent, and Havas ould become the leading shareholder in Canal Plus with 34.4 percent as part of a restructuring of their media activities.
German shares also surged to a new bourse record, buoyed by the dollar climbing to 1.66 marks and a stable German debt market.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade over one percent higher, just shy of record trading levels. The DAX-30 ended at 3,138.01 points, up 33.87. CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6641 marks and 124.21 yen compared with 1.6514 marks and 123.70 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 15.5 points, or 0.36 percent, at 4,2781.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 15.13 points, or 0.59 percent, at 2,573.56.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 33.87 points, or 1.09 percent, at 3,138.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.90 against $342.80 previously, the lowest fix since April 22, 1993. Silver was two cents down at $4.80.
